value.name: Miles worries about his future
value.description: Miles looks at the chessboard and fears ending up alone and medically ruined instead of having a family.
evidence: MILES Do you think I'm going to end up like Herb Myerson, with a colostomy bag instead of a family?

value.name: Kenneth questions Miles's symptoms
value.description: Kenneth asks whether Miles has symptoms after hearing his complaint about losing pleasure in life.
evidence: MILES Yes. The inability to experience pleasure.

value.name: Kenneth warns against moving the queen too early
value.description: Kenneth gives Miles chess advice, telling him not to waste time on his queen too soon.
evidence: KENNETH Oh. (beat) Don't waste time with your queen.
KENNETH The Center Counter Defense. The thing is not to move your queen too early.

value.name: Miles questions Marilyn's feelings
value.description: Miles shifts from chess to asking whether Marilyn Rexroth could really love Howard Doyle.
evidence: MILES She can't really love that idiot, can she?
MILES Marylin Rexroth. She came into my office and signed a pre-nup with Howard Doyle.

value.name: Kenneth identifies the Doyle marriage as real
value.description: Kenneth recognizes Howard Doyle and the Massey pre-nup, concluding that Marilyn must love him.
evidence: A Massey Pre-nup? (Miles nods again) She loves him.

value.name: Miles objects to Howard as the wrong man
value.description: Miles insists Howard is not the right man for Marilyn, revealing his judgment and concern about her relationship.

value.name: Kenneth warns Miles about misplaced romantic focus
value.description: Kenneth extends the chess metaphor into life, telling Miles not to waste time on someone else's queen.
evidence: KENNETH Miles! Don't waste time with someone else's queen, either.
